_comment: Illustrative, fictional content for `python main.py --demo`. Not real news.
key_points: Energy is the common thread: tighter LNG supply is pushing European utilities toward longer Asian-indexed contracts, while shipping rates for older tankers hit records.
Central banks are split: the Fed signals patience while the ECB hints at one more cut, widening the rate differential that supports the dollar.
Semiconductor export controls are shifting from chips to equipment servicing, a change that affects installed capacity rather than just new orders.
Fiscal pressure is building in the UK and France, where budget debates are running into bond market limits.

items.headline: Older supertankers now trade above new builds
items.context: Sanctions and rerouting have lengthened voyages, while the order book for new crude carriers remains at multi-decade lows.
items.impact: Higher freight costs feed into delivered oil prices and widen regional crude spreads, benefiting owners of legacy fleets at the expense of refiners.
items.conclusion: Watch newbuild orders at Asian yards: a surge would signal owners expect the premium to last beyond 2028.
items.original_title: Value of old supertankers soars past new builds

items.headline: Private credit outflows slow after a turbulent quarter
items.context: Redemption requests at semi-liquid private credit funds spiked after several high-profile defaults in leveraged software loans.
items.impact: Slower withdrawals reduce forced selling, but managers are still gating funds, which keeps a lid on new lending to mid-market companies.
items.conclusion: The asset class is stabilising, not recovering; default rates in Q4 remain the key test.
items.original_title: Private credit turmoil eases as investor withdrawals slow

items.headline: Talks over the Strait of Hormuz stall after US rejects reopening plan
items.context: Roughly a fifth of global oil supply transits the strait, which has faced intermittent disruption since the conflict began.
items.impact: A prolonged impasse keeps a risk premium in crude and LNG prices and pushes Asian importers to draw on strategic reserves.
items.conclusion: Any shift toward mediated talks would likely compress energy prices quickly; absent that, expect volatility around each diplomatic signal.
items.original_title: Iranian minister says only negotiation can end conflict

items.headline: South Korea launches a nationwide AI adoption programme
items.context: Seoul is pairing public compute subsidies with incentives for small manufacturers to deploy AI in production lines.
items.impact: The plan supports domestic demand for memory chips and positions Korean conglomerates as integrators, not just component suppliers.
items.conclusion: Execution risk is high, but the policy signals a shift from hardware exports to domestic AI services.
items.original_title: South Korea bets big on AI for all

items.headline: Alternatives to GPS move toward commercial deployment
items.context: Jamming and spoofing of satellite navigation have risen sharply near conflict zones, affecting aviation and shipping.
items.impact: Quantum and LEO-based positioning systems could become critical infrastructure, opening a defence-adjacent market for navigation suppliers.
items.conclusion: Regulatory certification for aviation will set the pace of adoption more than the technology itself.
items.original_title: Alternatives to GPS are around the corner
